apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: vuoro-tenant-controller, namespace: vuoro-system}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy: {type: Recreate}
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vuoro-tenant-controller}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vuoro-tenant-controller}
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: vuoro-tenant-controller
      imagePullSecrets: [{name: vuoro-ghcr-pull}]
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 65532, runAsGroup: 65532, fsGroup: 65532, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
      containers:
        - name: controller
          image: ghcr.io/bayleafwalker/vuoro-cloud@sha256:02b792fdf2324ad56ea3ae7a85e82c348b88ae00894bc2991c678f5b065875bf
          command: [vuoro-tenant-controller]
          env:
            - {name: VUORO_CLOUD_SERVICE_ROLE, value: controller}
            # The runtime pod's MCP container (D-046). Turn on only together with
            # a runtime image that ships vuoro-mcp-edge (`vuoro-service mcp-serve`).
            - {name: VUORO_CLOUD_TENANT_MCP_EDGE, value: "true"}
            # DB role split (unit 1.5, G2b): the control database as
            # vuoro_controller. Since G4 vuoro-controller-runtime carries no
            # VUORO_CLOUD_DATABASE_URL; this entry is the controller's only
            # control-database connection string.
            # The G2 explicit override from vuoro-tenant-provisioner-db is
            # the controller's only tenant-admin URL.
            - {name: VUORO_CLOUD_DATABASE_URL, valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: vuoro-controller-db, key: VUORO_CLOUD_DATABASE_URL}}}
          envFrom: [{secretRef: {name: vuoro-controller-runtime}}]
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 192Mi}
            limits: {cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi}
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: compatibility, mountPath: /app/config, readOnly: true}
      volumes:
        - {name: compatibility, configMap: {name: vuoro-compatibility}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata: {name: vuoro-tenant-controller, namespace: vuoro-system}
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata: {name: vuoro-tenant-controller}
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [namespaces]
    verbs: [get, create, patch]
  # The controller binds itself to vuoro-tenant-workspace inside each
  # vuoro-ws-* namespace; the admission policy confines where it may do so.
  - apiGroups: [rbac.authorization.k8s.io]
    resources: [rolebindings]
    verbs: [get, create, patch]
  - apiGroups: [rbac.authorization.k8s.io]
    resources: [clusterroles]
    verbs: [bind]
    resourceNames: [vuoro-tenant-workspace]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata: {name: vuoro-tenant-controller}
roleRef: {apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io, kind: ClusterRole, name: vuoro-tenant-controller}
subjects: [{kind: ServiceAccount, name: vuoro-tenant-controller, namespace: vuoro-system}]
---
# Everything the controller does inside a workspace namespace. Deliberately
# not bound cluster-wide: the controller binds it per vuoro-ws-* namespace
# (tenant.workspace_role_binding). Server-side apply needs get/create/patch;
# `kubectl wait` and `kubectl rollout status` additionally list/watch.
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata: {name: vuoro-tenant-workspace}
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [serviceaccounts, resourcequotas, limitranges, configmaps, secrets, services]
    verbs: [get, create, patch]
  - apiGroups: [apps]
    resources: [deployments]
    verbs: [get, list, watch, create, patch]
  - apiGroups: [batch]
    resources: [jobs]
    verbs: [get, list, watch, create, patch]
  - apiGroups: [networking.k8s.io]
    resources: [networkpolicies]
    verbs: [get, create, patch]
